description: Kernels have no band/bor/bxor/bnot/bsl/bsr (Bitwise module, or the Erlang :erlang.band/2 etc. forms), so hashing and checksum algorithms (CRC32, xxHash, FNV) can't be written; this blocks the checksum example defk-9p6.2. Support them on i64 with Elixir semantics: bsl/bsr are arithmetic with negative shift reversing direction, bsl on i64 must raise or match Elixir for results outside i64 (Elixir has bignums; decide: raise ArithmeticError on overflow like + - *), bnot is two's complement. Accept both `import Bitwise` operator forms (&&&, |||, ^^^, <<<, >>>, ~~~) and band/2-style calls. Tests compare with Elixir, including negative values and shift edge cases (shift >= 64, negative shift).

comments.text: Per 'Should kernels offer opt-in wrapping integer arithmetic for hashes?' (defk-dtw.10): scope now also covers masked arithmetic (band(expr, 2^k-1) with + - * bsl band bor bxor bnot inside, computed wrapping; bsr/div/rem only on in-range values; syntactic recognition), the u64 scalar and [u64] element type with its mixing rules, and Defk.Bits (clz, ctz, popcount, rotl, rotr). See the resolution comment on defk-dtw.10.

Per review of wave 1 (defk-vku): when bitwise operators land, add vku's targeted hint for `(1 <<< n) - 1` with n reaching 64 overflowing i64 (hint: the mask is often redundant when the value already fits n bits, or use masked arithmetic with a constant mask), with a test.
Promoted in importance by the 1BRC epic defk-n4r: it blocks word loads (defk-n4r.2) and the 1BRC kernel (defk-n4r.6); every byte-level text workload needs it. Consider raising to P1.

Now also blocks the Monte Carlo (defk-9p6.17), hash-chain (defk-9p6.18), codec (defk-9p6.19), hash (defk-9p6.20), CSV loader (defk-9p6.21) and UTF-8 (defk-9p6.22) catalog entries: eleven tickets in total. Recommend P1.
Also blocks the from-scratch epic defk-52v (keccak, blake, lz4/snappy, geohash/crc, the builtins ticket, inflate, argon2id). The count is now about twenty tickets.

Merged 2026-10-09 (a90829f). docs/language.md entry to add once defk-sgw.1 lands: "### Bitwise operators. On i64: band(a, b), bor, bxor, bnot(a), bsl(a, n), bsr(a, n), also written a &&& b, |||, ^^^, ~~~a, <<<, >>>, or Bitwise.band(a, b); no import Bitwise is needed. band/bor/bxor/bnot are two-complement; bsl/bsr shift exactly: a negative shift goes the other way, bsr fills with the sign (a shift of 64 or more gives 0 or -1), and bsl raises ArithmeticError when the exact result does not fit in i64 (a limit). Operands must be i64 (operand-type otherwise). band with a constant mask lets table[band(h, 255)] skip its bounds check. Elixir 1.20 deprecates ~~~ and ^^^; prefer bnot/1 and bxor/2." Retired code: bitwise (never reused); new code: shift-overflow.

title: Support bitwise operators in kernels
